## Agentic science: blessing or curse?

- Where do agents save us work, and where do they create new work?
- How do we set them up, steer them, and fence them in?
- Can we explain and defend every result we put our name on?

## The agent loop

```{=latex}
\centering
\begin{tikzpicture}[>=Latex,
 box/.style={draw=petroltrr,rounded corners,minimum width=2.6cm,minimum height=.8cm,align=center,font=\small}]
\node[box,fill=inputfill] (goal) at (-4.5,0) {Goal + constraints};
\node[box,fill=modelfill] (model) at (-1.3,0) {Model decides};
\node[box,fill=toolfill] (tool) at (2,0) {Tool executes};
\node[box,fill=inputfill] (obs) at (2,-1.6) {Observe result};
\node[box] (stop) at (-1.3,-1.6) {Stop / ask / deliver};
\draw[->,thick] (goal)--(model);
\draw[->,thick] (model)--(tool);
\draw[->,thick] (tool)--(obs);
\draw[->,thick] (obs.west)--(stop.east);
\draw[->,thick] (obs.east)--++(.5,0)--++(0,2.7)-|(model.north);
\end{tikzpicture}
```

An AI agent is an AI model operating in a loop: it reasons, calls tools, observes results, and repeats until a task is complete


## Some terms

```{=latex}
\small
```

| Term | Role | Example |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Instructions | Define goals, behavior, and constraints | System prompt, agent rules |
| Model | Generates responses and selects actions | GPT, Claude |
| Tools | Perform actions or retrieve information | Shell, web search, SQL query |
| MCP | Model Context Protocol: standardizes access to external tools and data | GitHub MCP server |
| Harness | Runs the model–tool loop and manages execution | Codex CLI, Claude Code |
| Framework | Provides components for building agents | LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK |

: {tbl-colwidths="[20, 50, 30]"}

A short shell script restarts a fresh agent until it replies DONE and the documents compile


## AI as an RA: a ladder of AI use

**The “Paul Goldsmith-Pinkham ladder of AI use”**

```{=latex}
\begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
\begin{column}{.78\textwidth}
\begingroup\footnotesize
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.35}
\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\centering\arraybackslash}p{.65cm}p{8.9cm}@{}}
\textbf{Level} & \textbf{What it looks like} \\ \hline
0 & Copy code from browser chat into your IDE \\
1 & IDE offers inline completions and inline chat \\
2 & IDE agent mode reads files, runs tests, and refactors \\
3 & Dedicated coding agents: Claude Code, Codex CLI, \ldots \\
4 & Attach tools: web search, scraping, browsing, orchestration \\
5 & Orchestrate teams of agents in containers
\end{tabular}
\endgroup
\end{column}
\begin{column}{.20\textwidth}
\centering
\begin{tikzpicture}[>=Latex]
\draw[->,thick,petroltrr] (0,0)--(0,-3.15);
\node[rotate=90,font=\scriptsize] at (-.25,-1.58) {Coding speed};
\draw[->,thick,yellowtrr] (.9,0)--(.9,-3.15);
\node[rotate=90,font=\scriptsize] at (1.15,-1.58) {Verification debt};
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{column}
\end{columns}
```


## Verification debt: the downside of faster coding

**Technical-debt analogy:** code produced quickly can create future maintenance work

```{=latex}
\begin{beamercolorbox}[rounded=true,sep=.7em,wd=\linewidth]{block body}
\textbf{Verification debt:} AI-generated code that has not yet been verified by the humans responsible for the project
\end{beamercolorbox}
```

- Agents can generate large code bases with little human intervention
- Their abstractions and coding style can differ from familiar research scripts
- Code that runs and looks professional can still be difficult to verify

**The relevant saving is time after review, correction, and rerunning**


## Some tips for basic agent use

```{=latex}
% Long list: less space between items on this slide only.
\renewcommand{\tightlist}{\setlength{\itemsep}{.3em}\setlength{\parskip}{0pt}}
```

1. Create a separate project copy or Git branch; record the starting state
2. Make sure that the project folder does not contain any sensitive data 
   (e.g., API keys, WRDS credentials, ...)
3. Include an informative README.md (like you would do for humans) that 
   describes the overall purpose of the project and its workflow
4. Add an AGENTS.md outlining how the agent should act on the project
5. Check that the required toolchain (data access, Python/R, shell commands)
   is available
6. Start with limited agent permissions and a small, inspectable task
7. Review the diff and rerun the analysis before accepting/committing the result

**A useful first instruction/task:** "Map the project and propose an audit plan."


## Context and memory need maintenance

- Update README.md to reflect the development of the project, always target it
  to the human reader
- Update AGENTS.md to reflect project conventions and reproducible commands
- Break long tasks into batches/stages with concrete deliverables
- Keep a CHANGES.md to document project history. Try to keep the other files
  focused on the current state (this is surprisingly hard)
- Agentic code bloats. Try to keep it clean and parsimonious


## A sandbox limits the reach of mistakes

```{=latex}
\centering
\begin{tikzpicture}[x=1cm,y=1cm,scale=.66,transform shape,>=Latex,
  block/.style={draw,rounded corners=3pt,minimum height=.67cm,align=center,font=\small},
  arr/.style={-Latex,thick},
  lab/.style={font=\scriptsize,align=center}]

% Task, outside the container.
\node[block,fill=inputfill,draw=inputedge,minimum width=3.0cm] (goal) at (0,0) {Research task};

% Sandboxed execution environment: the main new concept.
\draw[rounded corners=9pt,dashed,very thick,draw=modeledge,fill=modelfill!12]
  (-4.70,-.90) rectangle (4.70,-4.65);
\node[font=\bfseries\small,text=black!70] at (-2.5,-1.20) {ISOLATED CONTAINER};

\node[block,fill=modelfill,draw=modeledge,minimum width=3.15cm] (agent) at (0,-2.01) {AI agent};
\node[block,fill=toolfill,draw=tooledge,minimum width=2.85cm] (tools) at (-2.10,-3.38) {Tools: Python / shell};
\node[block,fill=toolfill,draw=tooledge,minimum width=2.85cm] (work) at (2.10,-3.38) {Scratch workspace};

\draw[arr] (goal) -- (agent);
\draw[arr] (agent.south) -- ++(0,-.37) -| (tools.north);
\draw[arr] (agent.south) -- ++(0,-.37) -| (work.north);

% External research files; only an explicit read-only mount is allowed.
\node[block,fill=restrictedfill,draw=restrictededge,minimum width=3.6cm] (original) at (0,-5.77) {Original research data};
\draw[arr,dashed,draw=modeledge] (original.north) -- (0,-4.65);
\node[lab,fill=white,inner sep=2pt] at (1.37,-5.06) {read-only mount\\(if configured)};
\node[lab,text=redtrr] at (-3.2,-5.78) {No broad host access};

\end{tikzpicture}


```

**Restrict mounts, credentials, and network access; keep outputs in a scratch area**

::: notes
1.5 minutes. Adapted from container_security.qmd. A container is one isolation layer, not a guarantee: broad host mounts or privileged execution defeat the boundary. Read-only access protects integrity but can still expose confidential content.
:::

## Keep the human (you) in the loop

- **Decide what the agent is allowed/supposed to do**: Outsource chores and not
  the intellectual core of your project
- **Formalize your workflow**: Define verification steps and document them in 
  AGENTS.md
- **Test systematically**: Learn the basics of software test suites and write 
  tests the agent must pass
- **Retain control**: Require human approval of changes 
  (e.g., *only humans commit*)
- **Verify crucial bits independently**: Verify the key results of the project
  by verifying them manually


## Could you defend the result without the agent?

Before accepting a contribution, can you explain:

- Which data and transformations produced it?
- Why the implementation matches the intended research design?
- Which checks passed, and which limitations remain?
- What you changed after reviewing the agent's work?


## When does a second agent help?

**Typical division:** one agent writes an audit and another checks its output against the task

- Give each role a bounded task and explicit evidence to inspect
- Avoid simultaneous edits to the same files
- Reconcile disagreements against data and executable checks

**Tradeoff:** parallel work can save time while increasing cost and coordination work

**Agreement among agents does not verify your code**

3. What would you expect from an AI-assisted coauthor?


## Where will this lead? Three speculative scenarios

```{=latex}
\small
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.4}
\begin{tabular}{@{}p{2.25cm}p{4.9cm}p{5.25cm}@{}}
\textbf{Scenario} & \textbf{Potential gain} & \textbf{Main concern} \\ \hline
\textbf{AIs check AIs} & Reproducible pipelines get second-opinion AI audits; faster validation & Unclear human role; shared blind spots and unknown unknowns \\
\textbf{Humans check AIs} & Human verification is built into research and review; responsibility is documented & Human attention remains a bottleneck; progress can be slower \\
\textbf{Nobody checks AIs} & Lower immediate production costs without transparent pipelines & Verification becomes costly or impossible; debt grows and peer review comes under pressure
\end{tabular}
```

**A possible side effect:** greater demand for research with visible, documented human intervention

# Some (arbitrary and incomplete) pointers

## Agent skills: get feedback on your research {.smaller}

- [AI Research Feedback](https://github.com/claesbackman/AI-research-feedback)
  — Referee-style paper reviews, identification checks, paper–code
  consistency, and adversarial code audits
- [MixtapeTools](https://github.com/scunning1975/MixtapeTools)
  — Scott Cunningham's workflows for empirical research, code audits,
  replication, presentations, and research management
- [Awesome Econ AI Stuff](https://github.com/meleantonio/awesome-econ-ai-stuff)
  — Reusable skills for econometrics, data cleaning, Stata, R, Python,
  and academic writing


## Connect agents to your research tools {.smaller}

- [Stata MCP](https://github.com/hanlulong/stata-mcp)
  — Let coding agents execute Stata commands and do-files, inspect
  results, and iterate on analysis code
- [EdgarTools](https://github.com/dgunning/edgartools)
  — Python tools and agent integrations for SEC filings, XBRL
  financials, and corporate disclosures
- [Zotero MCP](https://github.com/54yyyu/zotero-mcp)
  — Connect agents to your reference library, papers, and annotations



## Agent systems: automate research workflows (use at your own risk) {.smaller}

- [Claude Code Academic Workflow](https://github.com/pedrohcgs/claude-code-my-workflow)
  — Pedro Sant'Anna's ready-to-fork setup for academic projects,
  with specialized agents, review loops, and quality gates
- [PaperQA2](https://github.com/Future-House/paper-qa)
  — Literature research agent that retrieves evidence from papers
  and generates cited answers
- [data-to-paper](https://github.com/Technion-Kishony-lab/data-to-paper)
  — Research agent system linking data analysis, generated results,
  and manuscript text with traceability
